readout_other: serum cytokine panel (LEGENDplex 13-plex; TNF-alpha primary outcome); vagus nerve histology (H&E)
direction_notes: uVNS reduced serum TNF-alpha levels (single application ~19% reduction, triple application ~73% reduction vs. no-stimulation controls), interpreted as activation of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory reflex; direct neural activation (action potentials) was not recorded, and the effect was abolished by distal efferent vagotomy.
safety_notes: Histology of 8 vagus nerve specimens showed no significant lesions except mild, clinically insignificant multifocal neutrophil infiltration of the perineurium in one animal; temperature increased on average to a maximum of 2C over the 5-min stimulation.

timing.protocol_description: Focused ultrasound was delivered for 5 min per stimulation session, applied to the surgically exposed left vagus nerve via a coupling cone and ultrasound gel. Animals received either a single stimulation (u1VNS) or three stimulations (u3VNS, u3Vx) at t=30, 90 and 150 min relative to LPS injection.

source_quotes.n_subjects: We divided animals into five groups: no stimulation with LPS (nVNS, n = 11), single ultrasound stimulation with LPS $( \mathrm { u } _ { 1 } \mathrm { V N S } , \mathrm { n } = 1 1 )$ , triple ultrasound stimulation with LPS $( \mathrm { u } _ { 3 } \mathrm { V N S } , \mathrm { n } = 8 )$ , triple ultrasound stimulation with LPS and efferent fiber cervical vagotomy $( \mathrm { u } _ { 3 } \mathrm { V } \mathrm { x } ,$ n = 4) and electrical stimulation with LPS (eVNS, n = 5).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Control animals (nVNS) received no stimulation, single-stimulation (eVNS and $\mathbf { u } _ { 1 } \mathrm { V N S } )$ animals received stimulation only at t = 30, and triple-stimulation (u VNS) animals received stimulation at t = 30, 90 and 150.

flags.reason: Paper never states a combined total for ultrasound-exposed animals; group sizes for the three uVNS groups (u1VNS=11, u3VNS=8, u3Vx=4) are listed instead of summed.

Intensity was measured with a hydrophone in water at the focus but described in the text as the intensity 'applied to the vagus nerve'; since the nerve was surgically exposed and coupled with gel (no skull path), this was treated as a free-field measurement, but the paper does not explicitly state the domain.
Paper does not state whether animals were randomly allocated to groups.
